results.transcript: What is the difference between a virus and a bacterium and why do antibiotics only work on one of them?
results.reply: Viruses are tiny particles that need a host cell to replicate, while bacteria are single-celled organisms that can grow and divide on their own. Antibiotics target features like cell walls or protein-making machinery that only bacteria have, so they kill or stop bacteria but not viruses.
